definition.description:
Withdraw a task suggestion you queued earlier with spawn_task.

Call this when a suggestion has gone stale: the issue was fixed in this session (by you or the user), it turned out not to be a problem after all, or you have queued a better-scoped replacement — in that case queue the replacement with spawn_task first, then dismiss the old task_id.

Only a suggestion the user hasn't acted on can be withdrawn. If they already started, dismissed or edited it, the result says so and nothing changes; that answer is final, so don't retry or re-flag it.

Read the result before you start the task anew or do it here: after "Not withdrawn", don't start it anew, and do it here only if the user asks for that in chat.

reason.description: Optional short note on why the suggestion is no longer needed, e.g. "fixed in this session" or "superseded by task_ab12cd34". It doesn't change the outcome.

task_id.description: The task_id from the spawn_task result that queued the suggestion (of the form task_1a2b3c4d).

definition.name: mcp__ccd_session__dismiss_task

definition.description:
Suggest a separate task for something you noticed that is outside the scope of your current work.

Call this when you come across something that deserves fixing but doesn't belong in this change — dead code, stale docs, a missing test, a confirmed TODO, a bug or security issue spotted in passing. Don't use it for trivial fixes you can make inline, for anything the user asked you to do, for vague code-smell impressions or unverified hunches, or to split off parts of your own task. The call only queues a suggestion and returns; carry on with your current work.

The user sees a "Suggested task" card in the Claude desktop app with your title and tldr, can open the full prompt, and with one click starts it as a new session — on their machine in their local clone of this repository (optionally a fresh worktree of it), or in the cloud — sends it to this session, or dismisses it. A new session starts from your prompt alone, on a checkout that may not have this session's changes, so the prompt has to stand alone: what to change and why, the files involved by repository-relative path, and any context from this conversation it depends on. Absolute paths and other state of this environment may not exist there. If the find involves a secret or credential, say where it is rather than copying the value, since the prompt is stored and displayed.

The result carries a task_id; if the suggestion later becomes moot, withdraw it with dismiss_task.

prompt.description: The opening message of the new session: the goal, the files involved by repository-relative path, the context it needs from this conversation, and what done looks like. The user can read it in full before starting; markdown is fine. Keep it to what the task needs (hard limit 32000 characters) — the new session can read the code itself.

title.description: The card's heading and the new session's title: a short imperative phrase starting with a verb, under 60 characters, that makes sense on its own — e.g. "Fix stale README badge", "Remove dead config option".

tldr.description: One or two plain sentences on what the task would do and why it is worth doing. Shown on the card under the title; it is what the user reads when deciding whether to start it, so no file paths or code.

geometry) in the art of the user's approved original (images 2..: style / material references). Every job is logged with its
inputs (sha256), prompt, request id, estimated cost and outputs in <out>/<name>.job.json and appended to the ledger.

usage: python3 -I tools/lead21/fal_view.py <out_dir> <name> <prompt.txt> <structure.png> <ref.png> [ref2.png ...]
env: FAL_RES (2K), FAL_N (1), FAL_AR (9:16)"""
import base64, hashlib, io, json, os, subprocess, sys, time
from pathlib import Path
from PIL import Image

PRICE = {"0.5K": 0.06, "1K": 0.08, "2K": 0.12, "4K": 0.16}   # USD per output image (fal model page, 2026-11-20)
LEDGER = Path("/home/user/rainbow-/qa/review_r21/artwork/LEDGER.md")
out, name, prompt_f = Path(sys.argv[1]), sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3]
imgs = sys.argv[4:]
res, n, ar = os.environ.get("FAL_RES", "2K"), int(os.environ.get("FAL_N", "1")), os.environ.get("FAL_AR", "9:16")
out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
prompt = Path(prompt_f).read_text().strip()

def data_uri(p):
    im = Image.open(p).convert("RGB")
    b = io.BytesIO(); im.save(b, "JPEG", quality=94)
    return "data:image/jpeg;base64," + base64.b64encode(b.getvalue()).decode()

def curl(args, data=None):
    cmd = ["curl", "-sS", "--max-time", "180", "-H", "Authorization: Key proxy-injected"] + args
    r = subprocess.run(cmd, input=data, capture_output=True, text=True)
    if r.returncode: raise SystemExit(f"curl failed: {r.stderr[:300]}")
    return r.stdout

body = {"prompt": prompt, "image_urls": [data_uri(p) for p in imgs], "num_images": n, "aspect_ratio": ar,
        "resolution": res, "output_format": "png"}
t0 = time.time()
sub = json.loads(curl(["-H", "Content-Type: application/json", "--data-binary", "@-",
                       "https://queue.fal.run/fal-ai/nano-banana-2/edit"], json.dumps(body)))
rid = sub.get("request_id")
if not rid: raise SystemExit(f"submit failed: {json.dumps(sub)[:400]}")
status_url = sub.get("status_url") or f"https://queue.fal.run/fal-ai/nano-banana-2/requests/{rid}/status"
resp_url = sub.get("response_url") or f"https://queue.fal.run/fal-ai/nano-banana-2/requests/{rid}"
print("submitted", rid, flush=True)
st = {}
for _ in range(120):
    st = json.loads(curl([status_url]))
    if st.get("status") in ("COMPLETED", "FAILED", "ERROR", "CANCELLED"): break
    time.sleep(4)
res_j = json.loads(curl([resp_url]))
files = []
for i, im in enumerate(res_j.get("images", [])):
    dst = out / f"{name}_v{i + 1}.png"
    subprocess.run(["curl", "-sS", "--max-time", "180", "-o", str(dst), im["url"]], check=True)
    files.append(str(dst))
cost = PRICE.get(res, 0.12) * len(files)
job = {"name": name, "endpoint": "fal-ai/nano-banana-2/edit", "request_id": rid, "status": st.get("status"),
       "resolution": res, "aspect_ratio": ar, "num_images": n, "estimated_cost_usd": round(cost, 3),
       "inputs": [{"path": p, "sha256": hashlib.sha256(Path(p).read_bytes()).hexdigest()} for p in imgs],
       "prompt": prompt, "outputs": files, "seconds": round(time.time() - t0, 1),
       "error": None if files else json.dumps(res_j)[:600],
       "note": "PROPOSAL — generated view, NOT an approved reference until the user approves it"}
(out / f"{name}.job.json").write_text(json.dumps(job, indent=1))
LEDGER.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
if not LEDGER.exists():
    LEDGER.write_text("# Round 21 generated-artwork ledger (paid jobs, user-authorised 2026-11-20 ~02:20 UTC)\n\n"
                      "| UTC | job | endpoint | request id | images | est. cost (USD) | result |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n")
with LEDGER.open("a") as f:
    f.write(f"| {time.strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M', time.gmtime())} | {name} | nano-banana-2/edit {res} | `{rid}` | {len(files)} | "
            f"{cost:.2f} | {', '.join(Path(x).name for x in files) or 'FAILED: ' + (job['error'] or '')[:80]} |\n")
print(json.dumps({k: job[k] for k in ("name", "request_id", "status", "estimated_cost_usd", "outputs", "seconds", "error")}, indent=1))

"""paint06 step 3: full-screen plates for the five Screen 06 keyframes (k0 = the approved Screen 06 picture, k1..k4 = the
user's four storyboard panels). Each panel keeps its OWN pixels inside its registered window; only what lies outside the
panel (the phone frame is taller than a panel) + the HUD boxes (k0) + Benny's spot are painted by fal flux-pro fill, so a
Benny layer (the panel's own Benny pixels) can move when the player steers.
usage: python3 -I step3_plates.py prep|fill|up|comp <k...>"""
import json, sys
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
import cv2, numpy as np
from PIL import Image
sys.path.insert(0, '/home/user/rainbow-/tools/paint06')
R = '/home/user/rainbow-'; W = f'{R}/qa/match/06/paint06/work'
FW, FH = 864, 1536            # game frame
MX, MY = 112, 128             # plate margin (frame px) for pull-back + steering pan
PW, PH = FW + 2 * MX, FH + 2 * MY   # 1088 x 1792 (1x plate)
S = 1.5                       # final plate scale -> 1632 x 2688
REG = json.load(open(f'{W}/register.json'))
HUD_BOXES = [(26, 8, 840, 110), (124, 108, 742, 190)]   # painted HUD bar + stage banner on the approved picture (frame px)
RING = ((418, 1162), (300, 94))                           # waterline splash ring around Benny (frame px): centre, radii

def benny_alpha(scale=1.0, ring=True, dil=0):
    """Benny (BiRefNet matte of the approved picture) + splash-ring ellipse, frame coords * scale, float 0..1"""
    h, w = int(round(FH * scale)), int(round(FW * scale))
    m = np.asarray(Image.open(f'{W}/benny_matte_raw.png'))[..., 3].astype(np.float32) / 255
    full = np.zeros((FH, FW), np.float32); full[680:680 + m.shape[0], 120:120 + m.shape[1]] = m
    if dil: full = cv2.dilate(full, cv2.getStructuringElement(cv2.MORPH_ELLIPSE, (2 * dil + 1, 2 * dil + 1)))
    if ring:
        e = np.zeros((FH, FW), np.float32)
        cv2.ellipse(e, RING[0], RING[1], 0, 0, 360, 1.0, -1)
        e = cv2.GaussianBlur(e, (0, 0), 14)
        full = np.maximum(full, e)
    return cv2.resize(full, (w, h), interpolation=cv2.INTER_LINEAR)

def window(k, scale, src_scale=1.0, src=None):
    """warp keyframe k's own picture into plate coords at `scale`: returns rgb (float), coverage alpha"""
    pw, ph = int(round(PW * scale)), int(round(PH * scale))
    if k == 0:
        img = np.asarray(Image.open(src or f'{R}/references/06_crest_the_rinse_arch.png').convert('RGB')).astype(np.float32)
        A = np.array([[scale / src_scale, 0, MX * scale], [0, scale / src_scale, MY * scale]], np.float32)
    else:
        img = np.asarray(Image.open(src or f'{W}/panel{k}.png').convert('RGB')).astype(np.float32)
        if src:  # upscaled panel: resample to exactly 4x the panel size first
            w0, h0 = REG[str(k)]['size']; img = cv2.resize(img, (w0 * 4, h0 * 4), interpolation=cv2.INTER_AREA)
        M = np.array(REG[str(k)]['M'], np.float32)
        A = M.copy(); A[:, :2] /= src_scale; A *= scale; A[0, 2] += MX * scale; A[1, 2] += MY * scale
    rgb = cv2.warpAffine(img, A, (pw, ph), flags=cv2.INTER_CUBIC if scale / src_scale < 1.01 else cv2.INTER_AREA, borderMode=cv2.BORDER_REFLECT)
    cov = cv2.warpAffine(np.ones(img.shape[:2], np.float32), A, (pw, ph), flags=cv2.INTER_LINEAR, borderValue=0)
    return rgb, cov

def prep(k):
    rgb, cov = window(k, 1.0)
    inside = cov > 0.999
    inside = cv2.erode(inside.astype(np.uint8), np.ones((5, 5), np.uint8)).astype(bool)
    mask = ~inside
    if k == 0:
        for x0, y0, x1, y1 in HUD_BOXES: mask[MY + y0:MY + y1, MX + x0:MX + x1] = True
    b = np.zeros((PH, PW), np.float32); b[MY:MY + FH, MX:MX + FW] = benny_alpha(1.0, ring=True, dil=10)
    mask |= b > 0.12
    # context outside the window: heavily blurred reflection (fill repaints it anyway)
    ctx = rgb.copy(); bl = cv2.GaussianBlur(rgb, (0, 0), 25); ctx[mask] = bl[mask]
    Image.fromarray(ctx.clip(0, 255).astype(np.uint8)).save(f'{W}/k{k}_ctx.png')
    Image.fromarray((mask * 255).astype(np.uint8)).save(f'{W}/k{k}_mask.png')
    print(k, 'mask frac', round(mask.mean(), 3))

PROMPT = ("Seamless continuation of the same picture. Inside a giant glossy purple perforated washing-machine drum tunnel: "
          "rows of small rounded slots in shiny violet-magenta metal, broad polished copper-gold ring bands arching overhead with "
          "bright white highlight bars. A glowing turquoise, magenta and rainbow water slide with white sparkling light veins and "
          "soft white-lavender foam bubble clusters along its edges, a few iridescent soap bubbles. Vivid neon glossy cartoon 3D "
          "render, same lighting and colours. Calm open water where a character was, no character, no text, no UI, no logos.")

def fill(k):
    from fal import run, data_uri, download
    r = run('fal-ai/flux-pro/v1/fill', {'image_url': data_uri(f'{W}/k{k}_ctx.png'), 'mask_url': data_uri(f'{W}/k{k}_mask.png'),
            'prompt': PROMPT, 'output_format': 'png', 'safety_tolerance': '5', 'seed': 606 + k}, name=f'k{k}_fill', est_usd=0.05)
    download(r['images'][0]['url'], f'{W}/k{k}_fill.png'); print(k, 'fill', Image.open(f'{W}/k{k}_fill.png').size)

def up(k):
    from fal import run, data_uri, download
    r = run('fal-ai/seedvr/upscale/image', {'image_url': data_uri(f'{W}/k{k}_fill.png'), 'upscale_factor': 2}, name=f'k{k}_fill_up2', est_usd=0.1)
    download(r['image']['url'], f'{W}/k{k}_fill_up2.png'); print(k, 'up', Image.open(f'{W}/k{k}_fill_up2.png').size)

def comp(k):
    pw, ph = int(PW * S), int(PH * S)
    base = np.asarray(Image.open(f'{W}/k{k}_fill_up2.png').convert('RGB').resize((pw, ph), Image.LANCZOS)).astype(np.float32)
    if k == 0: rgb, cov = window(0, S, src_scale=2.0, src=f'{W}/appr06_seedvr2.png')
    else: rgb, cov = window(k, S, src_scale=4.0, src=f'{W}/panel{k}_seedvr4.png')
    a = (cov > 0.999).astype(np.float32)
    a = cv2.erode(a, np.ones((7, 7), np.uint8)); a = cv2.GaussianBlur(a, (0, 0), 3) * a
    if k == 0:
        for x0, y0, x1, y1 in HUD_BOXES:
            hb = np.zeros_like(a); hb[int((MY + y0) * S):int((MY + y1) * S), int((MX + x0) * S):int((MX + x1) * S)] = 1
            a = np.minimum(a, 1 - cv2.GaussianBlur(hb, (0, 0), 4))
    plate_a = a.copy()
    b = np.zeros_like(a); fy, fx = int(MY * S), int(MX * S)
    ba = benny_alpha(S, ring=True, dil=0); b[fy:fy + ba.shape[0], fx:fx + ba.shape[1]] = ba
    plate_a = np.minimum(plate_a, 1 - b)
    plate = base * (1 - plate_a[..., None]) + rgb * plate_a[..., None]
    Image.fromarray(plate.clip(0, 255).astype(np.uint8)).save(f'{W}/k{k}_plate.png')
    # Benny layer = this keyframe's OWN pixels where Benny + his splash ring are (moves with steering)
    lay = np.dstack([rgb, (b * a * 255)]).clip(0, 255).astype(np.uint8)
    ys, xs = np.where(b > 0.004); x0, x1, y0, y1 = xs.min(), xs.max() + 1, ys.min(), ys.max() + 1
    Image.fromarray(lay[y0:y1, x0:x1], 'RGBA').save(f'{W}/k{k}_benny.png')
    json.dump({'bbox_plate_px': [int(x0), int(y0), int(x1), int(y1)], 'plate_size': [pw, ph], 'scale': S, 'margin_frame_px': [MX, MY]},
              open(f'{W}/k{k}_benny.json', 'w'))

"""paint06: game capture vs the user's pictures. k0 vs references/06 (below the HUD strip = the live HUD covers the painted one);
k1..k4 vs the storyboard panel: (a) at the panel's own size (the game frame area-downscaled onto the panel), (b) in the game frame
(panel cubic-upscaled into its registered window). Pixels within 20 colour levels (max over RGB), the project's usual measure."""
import json, sys
import cv2, numpy as np
from PIL import Image
R = '/home/user/rainbow-'; W = f'{R}/qa/match/06/paint06/work'
shots = sys.argv[1]; fw_, fh_ = 864, 1536
reg = json.load(open(f'{W}/register.json'))
def load(p): return np.asarray(Image.open(p).convert('RGB')).astype(np.float32)
out = {}
for k in range(5):
    try: g = load(f'{shots}/06p{k}.png')
    except FileNotFoundError: continue
    if g.shape[1] != fw_: g = cv2.resize(g, (fw_, fh_), interpolation=cv2.INTER_AREA)
    if k == 0:
        a = load(f'{R}/references/06_crest_the_rinse_arch.png'); e = np.abs(g - a).max(axis=2)
        out['k0'] = {'below_hud_pct': round(100 * float((e[195:] <= 20).mean()), 1), 'whole_frame_pct': round(100 * float((e <= 20).mean()), 1)}
        continue
    p = load(f'{W}/panel{k}.png'); h, w = p.shape[:2]
    M = np.array(reg[str(k)]['M'], np.float64); sc = np.hypot(M[0, 0], M[1, 0])
    small = cv2.resize(g, (int(round(fw_ / sc)), int(round(fh_ / sc))), interpolation=cv2.INTER_AREA)
    b = cv2.warpAffine(small, cv2.invertAffineTransform((M / sc).astype(np.float32)), (w, h), flags=cv2.INTER_CUBIC)
    e = np.abs(b - p).max(axis=2)[4:-4, 4:-4]
    up = cv2.warpAffine(p, M.astype(np.float32), (fw_, fh_), flags=cv2.INTER_CUBIC)
    cov = cv2.erode((cv2.warpAffine(np.ones((h, w), np.float32), M.astype(np.float32), (fw_, fh_)) > 0.999).astype(np.uint8), np.ones((9, 9), np.uint8)).astype(bool)
    e2 = np.abs(g - up).max(axis=2)[cov]
    out[f'k{k}'] = {'panel_size_pct': round(100 * float((e <= 20).mean()), 1), 'game_frame_window_pct': round(100 * float((e2 <= 20).mean()), 1),
                    'window_share_of_screen_pct': round(100 * float(cov.mean()))}
    em = (np.abs(b - p).max(axis=2) > 20).astype(np.uint8) * 255
    Image.fromarray(em).save(f'{shots}/err_k{k}.png')
print(json.dumps(out, indent=1)); json.dump(out, open(f'{shots}/metrics.json', 'w'), indent=1)

"""paint06: game capture vs the user's pictures. k0 vs references/06 (below the HUD strip = the live HUD covers the painted one);
k1..k4 vs the storyboard panel: (a) at the panel's own size (the game frame area-downscaled onto the panel), (b) in the game frame
(panel cubic-upscaled into its registered window). Pixels within 20 colour levels (max over RGB), the project's usual measure."""
import json, sys
import cv2, numpy as np
from PIL import Image
R = '/home/user/rainbow-'; W = f'{R}/qa/match/06/paint06/work'
shots = sys.argv[1]; fw_, fh_ = 864, 1536
reg = json.load(open(f'{W}/register.json'))
def load(p): return np.asarray(Image.open(p).convert('RGB')).astype(np.float32)
out = {}
for k in range(5):
    try: g = load(f'{shots}/06p{k}.png')
    except FileNotFoundError: continue
    if g.shape[1] != fw_: g = cv2.resize(g, (fw_, fh_), interpolation=cv2.INTER_AREA)
    if k == 0:
        a = load(f'{R}/references/06_crest_the_rinse_arch.png'); e = np.abs(g - a).max(axis=2)
        out['k0'] = {'below_hud_pct': round(100 * float((e[195:] <= 20).mean()), 1), 'whole_frame_pct': round(100 * float((e <= 20).mean()), 1)}
        continue
    p = load(f'{W}/panel{k}.png'); h, w = p.shape[:2]
    M = np.array(reg[str(k)]['M'], np.float64); sc = np.hypot(M[0, 0], M[1, 0])
    small = cv2.resize(g, (int(round(fw_ / sc)), int(round(fh_ / sc))), interpolation=cv2.INTER_AREA)
    b = cv2.warpAffine(small, cv2.invertAffineTransform((M / sc).astype(np.float32)), (w, h), flags=cv2.INTER_CUBIC)
    e = np.abs(b - p).max(axis=2)[4:-4, 4:-4]
    up = cv2.warpAffine(p, M.astype(np.float32), (fw_, fh_), flags=cv2.INTER_CUBIC)
    cov = cv2.erode((cv2.warpAffine(np.ones((h, w), np.float32), M.astype(np.float32), (fw_, fh_)) > 0.999).astype(np.uint8), np.ones((9, 9), np.uint8)).astype(bool)
    e2 = np.abs(g - up).max(axis=2)[cov]
    out[f'k{k}'] = {'panel_size_pct': round(100 * float((e <= 20).mean()), 1), 'game_frame_window_pct': round(100 * float((e2 <= 20).mean()), 1),
                    'window_share_of_screen_pct': round(100 * float(cov.mean()))}
    em = (np.abs(b - p).max(axis=2) > 20).astype(np.uint8) * 255
    Image.fromarray(em).save(f'{shots}/err_k{k}.png')
print(json.dumps(out, indent=1)); json.dump(out, open(f'{shots}/metrics.json', 'w'), indent=1)

# Screen 06 — `?paint06=1`: the user's OWN pictures as the scenery (round 31, 2026-11-21, session branch `ccr-4fcad20e-a6pp8w`)

**User decision (2026-11-21 ~00:05 UTC, verbatim):** "Yes, do Screen 06 first … I want these exact. See these all these four images? I want exactly
those. Okay, 100%, or at least 95%." + "add any plugin or anything you need. I don't care how much it costs." (paid fal jobs authorised; ledger below).
This replaces the earlier rule "never paste the approved picture over the screen" FOR THIS TEST ONLY, on the user's explicit yes.
Targets: `references/06_crest_the_rinse_arch.png` (k0) + the four storyboard panels of `docs/briefs/2026-11-20-r30/USER_S06_STORYBOARD_R30.png` (k1..k4).

## How to see it
`/?paint06=1` (dev server) — play normally; Screen 06 shows the five pictures in order. QA checkpoints: `06p0` (= `06`, approved picture), `06p1`..`06p4`
(the four panels), `06p_in` (8 u before 06). Default build (switch off) = **pixel-identical** to before for 05 / 06 / 07 (verified 2026-11-21 ~00:45,
same checkout with / without the change, fonts served from a real node_modules copy).

## What it is (src/world/paint06.ts, hooks in src/game/Game.ts — all behind the switch)
* Five full-screen plates (1440×2400 = the 864×1536 frame ×1.25 + margins). Inside each panel's own window (registered onto the approved frame through the
  painted Benny every panel shares: SIFT, ≤1.6 px median error, `work/register.json`) the plate IS the panel: SeedVR2 ×4 detail, back-projected so its
  downscale equals the panel. Outside the panel (a phone frame is taller than a panel) + under Benny: fal flux-pro fill continuation, invented coins
  auto-detected and erased (bria eraser), colour-matched to the panel edge (no seam), panel edge pixels dropped (they mix with the sheet's white gutter).
* Each plate sits on a depth grid (Depth Anything v2): at its rest moment the view is the picture exactly; as Benny swims the view pushes toward that
  picture's tunnel end (near water grows faster than the far tunnel = real parallax).
* Benny = that picture's own painted Benny pixels (BiRefNet matte + splash ring) as a layer: steers left/right (60 px per unit), leans, bobs 2.5 px
  (zero at whole seconds). The 3D Benny is hidden while the painted one shows.
* Picture → picture: the next picture opens from its tunnel's far end as a growing circle with a soft 150 px edge (~0.95 s); no full-frame double image.
  05 → 06 and 06 → 07 joins: the same reveal between the live 3D game and the pictures.
* Speed through 06 × 0.33 (11 → 3.6 u/s): 06 lasts ~16 s instead of ~5 s, ~3 s per picture. Coins: the painted coins are scenery; the game's own
  (hidden) coins still count in the HUD as Benny passes them. Hearts / foam-wall bumps unchanged.
* Colours: raw bytes in → raw bytes out (no tone mapping, no grade, no bloom on the pictures).

## Numbers (live game captures, `shots/metrics.json`; pixels within 20 colour levels, the project's usual measure)
| moment | vs | result |
|---|---|---|
| k0 (`06p0`) | approved Screen 06 | 97.9 % below the HUD strip (the live HUD covers the painted one; whole frame 88.7 %) |
| k1 (`06p1`) | panel 1 | 97.7 % at the panel's own size |
| k2 (`06p2`) | panel 2 | 98.2 % |
| k3 (`06p3`) | panel 3 | 97.9 % |
| k4 (`06p4`) | panel 4 | 98.3 % |
"At the panel's own size" = the game frame downscaled onto the panel (the panels are only 491 px wide; at phone size the game is sharper than the
panel, so a bigger-size comparison would count added sharpness as difference). The panel covers 56–60 % of the phone screen; the rest is continuation.

## Proof (`proof/`)
`0_APPROVED06_vs_GAME.jpg`, `1..4_PANELk_vs_GAME.jpg` (your picture | game, full size), `SCREEN06_paint06_straight_1x.mp4` (one uninterrupted run
05 → all of 06 → into 07, 30 fps), `SCREEN06_paint06_steer_1x.mp4` (same with left/right steering).

## Honest differences
* Outside each panel's own area (the top ~17 % and bottom ~18 % of the phone screen, thin side strips) the scenery is a continuation in the same style,
  not the user's pixels (k0 = the approved picture covers the whole frame).
* Between the rest moments the picture is pushed forward (sharper near water, slight stretching at strong depth edges); the reveal edge mixes two
  pictures for under a second per change.
* The painted coins are not collected visually (no pop); the HUD counts the game's own coins.
* The 05 → 06 and 06 → 07 joins reveal the 3D Screens 05 / 07 as they are now (their own work is separate).

## Rebuild
`tools/paint06/`: `register_panels.py` → `step2_upscale_matte.py` (fal) → `step3_plates.py prep|fill|erase|up|comp 0 1 2 3 4` (fal for fill/erase/up)

--out=qa/match/06/paint06/shots`, `python3 -I tools/paint06/measure.py qa/match/06/paint06/shots`, clips `node tools/paint06/clip.mjs [--weave]`.
Paid jobs: `LEDGER.md` (31 fal jobs, ≈ US$1.76 estimated).

Screen 06 now shows your pictures in the running game: your approved Screen 06 picture first, then your four new pictures in order, while Benny swims and steers. Your normal game is untouched: with the test switched off, Screens 05, 06 and 07 are pixel-for-pixel the same as before. To try it, open the game with `?paint06=1` added to the address.

| 2. Descend through the gold band | 98.2% |
| 3. Follow the winding slide | 97.9% |
| 4. Connect into Screen 07 | 98.3% |

All five are above your 95%. The rest is fine edges, because the game is drawn sharper than your small pictures.

**How it plays:**
- The water, the purple walls, the gold bands, the coins, the bubbles and Benny are your pictures' own pixels.
- As Benny swims, the view glides forward into each picture: near water comes closer faster than the far tunnel.
- Each new picture opens up from the far end of the tunnel instead of a blurry double image.
- Benny steers left and right and leans.
- Benny swims slower through Screen 06, so each picture gets about 3 seconds instead of under one.

**What isn't exactly yours:**
- **Top and bottom of the screen:** your pictures are wider than a phone screen, so about a sixth at the top and bottom is a continuation I generated in the same style. You can see it in the comparison pictures: grey marks where your picture ends.
- **Picture changes:** each change takes about a second, and for that moment you see the edge where one picture meets the next.
- **Coins:** the painted coins don't pop when Benny passes them, but the coin counter still goes up.
- **Entering and leaving Screen 06:** you briefly see the current 3D Screens 05 and 07, which haven't had this treatment yet.

entries.description:
Check the Thrixel API key, the cube balance, and how many jobs are running. Call this before submitting a large batch so you can size it to the budget and the concurrency cap, and after a 'jobs already running' or 'out of cubes' error.

Costs: flat per run: detail 14, sculpt 8, texture 5, rig 5 cubes, plus a reference image when they are given only a prompt (about 3 for sculpt, 7 for detail / texture, which compose it from the model); reduce_triangles and transform are free, and so is choosing a texture size on download; create / edit are metered on actual model usage (tens of cubes, sometimes more). Concurrency is capped per plan; an admin account is unlimited. The cap only limits how many jobs you may have in flight: detail / sculpt / texture / rig share one GPU lane across the service, so a batch of them finishes over time whatever your cap. This reports that lane's depth.
entries.name: mcp__Thrixel__thrixel_account_status

entries.description:
Get a download link for a finished model in a specific format. The server converts the model first when that format has not been made yet.

Every format is available on every plan at no extra cost. GLB is the right choice for web and Three.js and is served directly; FBX, OBJ, STL and USDZ are converted on demand, so the first request for one takes longer.

BUILDING A THREE.JS OR BROWSER GAME: pass textures='webp'. Same model - same parts, same triangle count, same bounds - with WebP textures instead of PNG. Measured: a texture-heavy model goes 18.3MB -> 0.95MB, a geometry-heavy one 7.0MB -> 6.3MB. Browsers decode WebP natively, so there is nothing to install and nothing to wire up. Use it for every asset headed to a web page.

draco=True additionally compresses the GEOMETRY, which only pays off on models that are mostly geometry (6.3MB -> 1.2MB on the example above; about 4% on a texture-heavy one). It needs a Draco decoder on the other end: three.js requires DRACOLoader to be set up explicitly. A reader WITHOUT one does not error, it loads every vertex at the origin, so the failure surfaces later as an empty scene. Leave it off unless you know the consumer decodes Draco, and never use it for a model going into Unity, Unreal, a modelling tool, or back into another pipeline.

ROBLOX: download format='glb', target='roblox'. Roblox ignores a material's flat colour, so a plain Thrixel GLB or FBX imports grey; this GLB gives each part group one mesh and one colour texture, removes see-through glass and keeps every mesh under 20,000 triangles, and imports in colour as-is. Reduce the model first if the whole is over budget. Use the FBX zip below only for a humanoid that needs an R15 rig.

FBX FOR AN ENGINE: pass target='unity' or 'ue5' to get a rigged humanoid's bones named for that engine's humanoid skeleton, or target='roblox' for a .zip with the FBX as a Roblox R15 rig, 1024 px textures and a textures/ folder of PBR maps. Roblox does not apply an FBX's materials: in Studio, add a SurfaceAppearance to each MeshPart and set its maps from that folder (SurfaceAppearance.txt in the zip says which, including the emissive settings for glowing parts), or the model shows grey. Non-humanoid models get the same file as generic, except roblox still packs the maps.

SMALLER TEXTURES: pass texture_size=512, 1024 or 2048 to cap every texture's longest side at that many pixels, in any format with textures (GLB, FBX, OBJ, USDZ; STL has none). It only shrinks: a model whose textures are already that size or smaller comes back unchanged. Geometry is identical. Use it for a game's texture budget or a lighter file; it is free and is made once, then kept.

dest.description: Where to save, relative to the output directory (THRIXEL_OUTPUT_DIR, else ./thrixel_assets). A directory ("public/models") derives the filename from the model; a path ending in the format's extension writes exactly that file. Absolute paths are refused.
dest.title: Dest

draco.description: GLB only. Geometry compression. Only for consumers that decode it.
draco.title: Draco

format.description: One of glb, fbx, obj, stl, usdz.
format.title: Format

quality.description: GLB only. "full" (default): the complete model with all surface detail; right after a model finishes this can take a few minutes, and the call waits for it. "lite": a lightweight file with simplified surface colors, available as soon as the model is. A placeholder only: replace it with the full download later, and never edit its geometry locally, since the full build cannot be laid over those edits. Change shape on the server (edit, transform, reduce) instead.
quality.title: Quality

target.description: The engine the file is for. GLB: generic (default) or roblox (one mesh and one colour texture per part group, imports in colour). FBX: generic, roblox (a .zip with an R15 rig and textures/ for SurfaceAppearance), unity or ue5 (humanoid bone names for that engine).
target.title: Target

texture_size.description: 512, 1024 or 2048 to cap every texture's longest side at that many pixels. Only shrinks. Not for STL, which has no textures.
texture_size.title: Texture Size

textures.description: GLB only. "png" (default) or "webp". Use webp for the browser.
textures.title: Textures

entries.name: mcp__Thrixel__thrixel_download

entries.description:
Check whether a job has finished, and how long it has been running. Only needed for jobs submitted with wait=false - every other tool already waits and returns the finished asset.

A job can sit at queued for a long time while your own concurrency cap still reports free slots: detail, sculpt, texture and rig all share one GPU lane across the whole service, so your slots say nothing about how many jobs are ahead of yours. Waiting is normal. Resubmitting is not - it pays twice for the same asset.
entries.name: mcp__Thrixel__thrixel_job_status

entries.description:
List the projects on this account, newest first, with how many assets each holds. Free.

Use it to find the project_id for a game the user started earlier, then pass that id to thrixel_start_project to resume it.
entries.name: mcp__Thrixel__thrixel_list_projects

entries.description:
Create a dense, organic 3D model from a text description and/or a single reference image. Costs 8 cubes and runs on the shared GPU lane.

Cost detail: given only a prompt, a reference image is generated for the job and billed separately (about 3 cubes), so the call totals roughly 11. Supplying the image yourself, or reusing one with reference_image_id, skips that generation and costs 8.

HOW THE PROMPT IS USED: it is turned into ONE three-quarter-view picture of the object first, and that picture is turned into 3D. So describe only what a single picture shows, in one or two sentences: 'a mossy stone frog statue, squat, cracked grey stone'. Long prompts that describe the back, several objects, or where it is mounted make the result worse, not better. Starting from your own image skips the picture step.

Use this for creatures, characters, plants, rocks, food, cloth - anything sculpted rather than assembled - and whenever you are starting from a photo.

The output is ONE high-density textured mesh with NO separate parts, and that is permanent: nothing on it can be animated or moved independently later. So if any piece of the asset has to move on its own, use thrixel_create_model instead, even for an organic subject.

For a STATIC organic asset this beats thrixel_create_model followed by thrixel_detail_model on both looks and price: that chain is a metered create (tens of cubes) plus a flat 14, several times this tool.

The output carries base colour, metallic, roughness and alpha only: glowing or emissive materials need thrixel_create_model.

SIZE: the result arrives with a longest side of about 1 unit. Pass target_size_m for a real-world size, or resize it afterwards with thrixel_transform_model, which is free.

To make a whole set share one look, pass the same style_reference_submission_id to every call - a finished model carries a palette and a finish far better than repeating adjectives does. For rules rather than looks (polycount, naming, sizes), use thrixel_add_project_source instead; the two combine.

Waits for the job to finish, saves the GLB, and returns the file path plus a rendered thumbnail.

decimation_target.description: Maximum triangle count for the output mesh, 10000-250000. Set this when the asset has a game budget; otherwise leave it to the server. Below 10000 the request is rejected, so ask for 10000 and cut further with thrixel_reduce_triangles, which is free.
decimation_target.title: Decimation Target

dest.description: Where to save, relative to the output directory: THRIXEL_OUTPUT_DIR if set, else ./thrixel_assets under the server's working directory (results print the absolute folder). A path ending in .glb is the file to write ("units/keep.glb"); anything else is a directory ("units"). Absolute paths are refused. Validated at submission, so a bad path costs nothing.
dest.title: Dest

image.description: A single reference image: a path to a file on this machine (read and encoded for you), an http(s) URL, or a data: URI. A local path is the normal case - pass the file, do not encode it yourself. When both are supplied the image drives the shape and the prompt guides style.
image.title: Image

project_id.description: Override the active project for this one call. Normally omit it - thrixel_start_project sets the destination once.
project_id.title: Project Id

prompt.description: Text description of the object, one or two sentences about what a single three-quarter view shows. Required unless image is given.
prompt.title: Prompt

reference_image_id.description: The id of an image already in this account, used as the reference instead of generating one from the prompt. Passing the same id to every sculpt in a set keeps the set visually consistent.
reference_image_id.title: Reference Image Id

style_reference_submission_id.description: A finished submission whose look (palette, materials, wear, finish) this one should match. Pass the same id across a set and they read as one family. With `prompt` it steers the image generated from your text; with `image` it restyles YOUR image into that look, so the result is no longer the picture you passed in. It contributes appearance only - the subject always comes from your prompt or your image.
style_reference_submission_id.title: Style Reference Submission Id

target_size_m.description: Optional real-world size: the longest side in metres, between 0.01 and 1000. Omit for the default (longest side about 1). If the result reports a different size, resize it with thrixel_transform_model.
target_size_m.title: Target Size M

wait.description: Wait for completion (default). Set false to submit and return immediately with a submission_id to poll via thrixel_job_status. BATCH PATTERN: running several? Submit them all with wait=false, do other work, then poll. Stay within your concurrency cap, which thrixel_account_status reports; free jobs count toward it too.
wait.title: Wait

entries.name: mcp__Thrixel__thrixel_sculpt_model

entries.description:
Create a Thrixel project and make it the destination for everything generated afterwards, or reopen an existing one. Free.

CALL THIS FIRST, before generating anything, and name it after the game. Every model, edit, detail pass and texture pass from then on is filed under it automatically - you do not pass project_id anywhere. Without it, assets from every game the user has ever built land in one flat list, and there is no way to sort them out afterwards.

Pass `name` to create a new project. Pass `project_id` instead to resume one that already exists - use thrixel_list_projects to find it. Resuming is the right move when the user returns to a game they started earlier, so the new assets join the old ones.

Pass BOTH `project_id` and `name` to RENAME a project and resume it in the same call. Games get renamed mid-development; do this rather than creating a second project, which would split one game's assets across two folders. Only the label changes - every asset stays where it is.

The project is visible in the Thrixel web app, so the user can browse and edit that game's assets as a set.

description.description: Optional note stored with the project. Updates the note when passed alongside `project_id`.
description.title: Description

name.description: Name for a NEW project, or the new name when renaming an existing one (pass `project_id` too). Use the game's name.
name.title: Name

project_id.description: Activate this EXISTING project instead of creating one. Pass `name` as well to rename it in the same call.
project_id.title: Project Id

input.command:
mkdir -p qa/benny/r31/input && python3 -I - <<'EOF'
import sys, json; sys.path.insert(0,'tools/paint06')
from fal import run, data_uri, download
from PIL import Image
import numpy as np
O='qa/benny/r31/input'
im=Image.open('qa/match/06/paint06/work/appr06_seedvr2.png').convert('RGB').crop((330,1380,1340,2400)); im.save(f'{O}/benny_appr06_2x_crop.png')
r=run('fal-ai/birefnet/v2', {'image_url': data_uri(f'{O}/benny_appr06_2x_crop.png'), 'model':'General Use (Heavy)', 'output_format':'png', 'refine_foreground': True}, name='benny31_matte2x', est_usd=0.01)
download(r['image']['url'], f'{O}/benny_appr06_2x_rgba.png'); print('matte url', r['image']['url'])
a=np.asarray(Image.open(f'{O}/benny_appr06_2x_rgba.png').convert('RGBA'))
ys,xs=np.where(a[...,3]>128); x0,x1,y0,y1=xs.min(),xs.max(),ys.min(),ys.max(); print('bbox',x0,x1,y0,y1)
obj=Image.fromarray(a).crop((x0,y0,x1+1,y1+1)); w,h=obj.size; S=1024; sc=0.86*S/max(w,h)
obj=obj.resize((int(w*sc),int(h*sc)),Image.LANCZOS)
for bgname,bg in (('white',(255,255,255,255)),('alpha',(0,0,0,0))):
    c=Image.new('RGBA',(S,S),bg); c.alpha_composite(obj,((S-obj.size[0])//2,(S-obj.size[1])//2)); c.save(f'{O}/benny_input_{bgname}.png')
json.dump({'matte_url': r['image']['url'], 'crop_in_appr06_2x': [330,1380,1340,2400], 'bbox_in_crop':[int(x0),int(y0),int(x1),int(y1)], 'scale_to_input': sc}, open(f'{O}/input.json','w'), indent=1)
EOF

    al = im[..., 3] / 255; s, dx, dy = align(al)

contrast 1.15) is inverted numerically, so at the approved rear view the screen shows the approved pixels.

import io, json, struct, sys
import numpy as np, cv2
from PIL import Image
from scipy.spatial import cKDTree
sys.path.insert(0, '/home/user/rainbow-/tools/benny31')
from fit import align, A, FW, FH, WL
R = '/home/user/rainbow-'
glb, uvf, size, fitpng, out = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], int(sys.argv[3]), sys.argv[4], sys.argv[5]
K = float(sys.argv[6]) if len(sys.argv) > 6 else 4.0
TEX = 2048

# ---------------- forward colour chain (numpy copy of three r170 NeutralToneMapping + sRGB + src/render/grade.ts)
def neutral(c):
    c = c.copy(); x = c.min(axis=-1, keepdims=True)
    off = np.where(x < 0.08, x - 6.25 * x * x, 0.04); c = c - off
    peak = c.max(axis=-1, keepdims=True); sc = 0.76; d = 1 - sc
    newp = 1 - d * d / (peak + d - sc)
    comp = c * (newp / np.maximum(peak, 1e-6))
    g = 1 - 1 / (0.15 * (peak - newp) + 1)
    comp = comp * (1 - g) + newp * g
    return np.where(peak < sc, c, comp)

def grade(c):
    l = (c * np.array([0.2126, 0.7152, 0.0722])).sum(axis=-1, keepdims=True)
    col = l + (c - l) * 1.36; col = (col - 0.5) * 1.15 + 0.5
    return np.clip(col, 0, 1)
def forward(L): return grade(srgb(neutral(L * 0.86)))

# inverse by nearest neighbour on a dense grid + Gauss-Newton refinement
t = np.linspace(0, 1, 72) ** 2.0 * 6.0
G = np.stack(np.meshgrid(t, t, t, indexing='ij'), -1).reshape(-1, 3)
FG = forward(G); tree = cKDTree(FG)

    for _ in range(6):

        J = np.zeros((len(L), 3, 3)); h = 1e-3
        for k in range(3):
            Lk = L.copy(); Lk[:, k] += h; J[:, :, k] = (forward(Lk) - F0) / h
        dL = np.linalg.lstsq if False else None
        Jt = np.transpose(J, (0, 2, 1)); JtJ = Jt @ J + 1e-6 * np.eye(3); Jtr = (Jt @ r[..., None])[..., 0]
        L = np.clip(L + np.linalg.solve(JtJ, Jtr[..., None])[..., 0], 0, 6.0)
    return L

# ---------------- approved target colours at the fitted view
uvp = np.frombuffer(open(uvf, 'rb').read(), np.float32).reshape(size, size, 4)[::-1]   # rows top-down
al = np.asarray(Image.open(fitpng).convert('RGBA'))[..., 3].astype(np.float32) / 255
s, dx, dy = align(al); fs = al.shape[0] / size                     # fit render px -> frame px; uv px -> fit px
yy, xx = np.mgrid[0:size, 0:size].astype(np.float32)
fx = s * ((xx + 0.5) * fs - 0.5) + dx; fy = s * ((yy + 0.5) * fs - 0.5) + dy
appr2 = np.asarray(Image.open(f'{R}/qa/match/06/paint06/work/appr06_seedvr2.png').convert('RGB')).astype(np.float32) / 255
Am = cv2.erode((A > 0.5).astype(np.uint8), np.ones((3, 3), np.uint8))
inA = (fx >= 0) & (fx < FW - 1) & (fy >= 0) & (fy < WL - 2)
inA[inA] = Am[fy[inA].astype(int), fx[inA].astype(int)] > 0
sel = inA & (uvp[..., 3] > 0.5) & (uvp[..., 2] > 0.15)
D = cv2.remap(appr2, (2 * fx + 0.5).astype(np.float32), (2 * fy + 0.5).astype(np.float32), cv2.INTER_LINEAR)[sel]
L = inverse(D)
u = uvp[..., 0][sel]; v = uvp[..., 1][sel]; w = uvp[..., 2][sel] ** 2
tx = np.clip((u * TEX).astype(int), 0, TEX - 1); ty = np.clip((v * TEX).astype(int), 0, TEX - 1)
acc = np.zeros((TEX, TEX, 3)); wsum = np.zeros((TEX, TEX))
np.add.at(acc, (ty, tx), L * w[:, None]); np.add.at(wsum, (ty, tx), w)
print('approved samples', int(sel.sum()), 'texels hit', int((wsum > 0).sum()))

# ---------------- the model's own texture for everything else (as display colours -> same inversion)
b = open(glb, 'rb').read(); n = struct.unpack('<I', b[12:16])[0]; j = json.loads(b[20:20 + n]); bin0 = 20 + n + 8
bv = j['bufferViews'][j['images'][0]['bufferView']]
own = np.asarray(Image.open(io.BytesIO(b[bin0 + bv.get('byteOffset', 0): bin0 + bv.get('byteOffset', 0) + bv['byteLength']])).convert('RGB').resize((TEX, TEX), Image.LANCZOS)).astype(np.float32) / 255
hit = wsum > 0
Lb = np.zeros((TEX, TEX, 3)); Lb[hit] = acc[hit] / wsum[hit][:, None]
# colour-match the model's own texture to the baked approved colours where both exist (per-channel affine in display space)
Dap = forward(Lb[hit]); Down = own[hit]
Mfit = np.linalg.lstsq(np.c_[Down, np.ones(len(Down))], Dap, rcond=None)[0]
own_m = np.clip(np.c_[own.reshape(-1, 3), np.ones(TEX * TEX)] @ Mfit, 0, 1).reshape(TEX, TEX, 3)
Lown = inverse(own_m).reshape(TEX, TEX, 3)
# soft blend: approved bake where it has support (push-pull smoothed weight), the model's own colours elsewhere
wgt = cv2.GaussianBlur(np.minimum(1, wsum / 0.25).astype(np.float32), (0, 0), 3)
fillL = Lb.copy()
# fill bake holes inside its support by normalized convolution
num = cv2.GaussianBlur((Lb * (wsum > 0)[..., None]).astype(np.float32), (0, 0), 2); den = cv2.GaussianBlur((wsum > 0).astype(np.float32), (0, 0), 2)[..., None]
fillL = np.where((wsum > 0)[..., None], Lb, num / np.maximum(den, 1e-4))
wb = np.clip(wgt * 1.6, 0, 1)[..., None]
Lfin = fillL * wb + Lown * (1 - wb)
V = np.clip(Lfin / K, 0, 1)
Image.fromarray((srgb(V) * 255 + 0.5).astype(np.uint8)).save(out)
json.dump({'K': K, 'samples': int(sel.sum()), 'texels': int(hit.sum()), 'colour_match': Mfit.tolist()}, open(out + '.json', 'w'), indent=1)
print('baked ->', out)
EOF

    return np.frombuffer(b[off: off + a['count'] * nc * np.dtype(comp).itemsize], comp).reshape(a['count'], nc)
prim = j['meshes'][0]['primitives'][0]

nlab, lab = cv2.connectedComponents(isl, connectivity=8)

# blend weight = closeness to a REAL projected texel of the same island (no colour leaking across islands)

    num = cv2.GaussianBlur((Lb_i * h[..., None]).astype(np.float32), (0, 0), 2.0); den = cv2.GaussianBlur(h.astype(np.float32), (0, 0), 2.0)[..., None]
